ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (26) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form).

The opening plays on «наказывать» (nakazyvat'), which means 'to punish' but in its older sense 'to instruct, enjoin', and «поучать» (pouchat', 'to instruct'); it is kept literal ('To punish—in Russian means to instruct'). Matthew 18:21–22 and John 8:3–11 are translated from the Russian wording («седмижды семидесяти», sedmizhdy semidesyati, 'seven times seventy'), and the Slavonic «Мне отмщение, и аз воздам» (Mne otmshcheniye, i az vozdam, Romans 12:19) is 'Vengeance is mine, and I shall repay'; «Джеферсон» (Dzheferson) is Jefferson.
